sentence: This project studies how extracellular regulatory proteins link Notch signaling with other developmental pathways and engineers proteins that change Notch protein activity.
This project studies how DNA elements that interact with many other DNA areas control gene networks in T cell acute leukemia.
This project uses the small, transparent embryos of Ciona to study which genes let cells survive metamorphosis and how cells fuse.
This project builds extracellular matrix matrices that help stem cell derived neuronal models mature and age.
This project tests whether smartphone data collected in the background can detect neurobehavioral impairment in frontotemporal dementia and Alzheimer's disease.
This project supports clinical trials that aim to improve survival and quality of life for cancer patients.
This project studies why a myokine works less well in aging muscle and whether satellite cells secreting it can improve muscle repair.
This project studies how inhibition of tyrosine metabolism is linked to tuberculosis susceptibility.
This project develops and pilot tests an intervention to reduce lung cancer among Appalachian women together with community partners.
This project builds an automated microinjection system that uses computer vision to inject embryos from diverse species.
This project provides mass spectrometry tools that image and measure molecules, such as proteins and metabolites, in cancer cells and tissues.
This project studies how irradiating regional lymph nodes changes the anti-tumor immune response against head and neck cancer in animal models.
This project supports gene inactivation studies and analyzes genomics data to find regulators of lineage plasticity in lung and prostate cancer.
This project studies how the tetrapartite synapse in the brain affects the risk and consequences of heavy alcohol consumption.
This project studies how vitamin C dependent metabolic rewiring controls extracellular matrix synthesis and cell state transitions.
This project tests whether human organoids can predict how safe and efficient genome editing therapeutics are.
This project studies the role of fibroblast growth factor 21 in osteoporosis in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy.
This project uses cryogenic electron microscopy and nanodiscs to resolve structures of glycoproteins from Varicella-zoster virus.
This project studies how type IV pili, which are bacterial appendages, are regulated and how they work in Acinetobacter species.
This project uses biological models such as hibernating mammals and sled dogs to look at age-related conditions, particularly frailty and dementia.
